references.text: The same command to redeem the donkey's foal with a lamb, or break its neck, is found here in the original law concerning the firstborn.
Explains the background for the redemption of firstborn sons, linked to the exodus from Egypt.
The command to give the firstborn to the Lord, which forms the basis for the obligation of redemption.
A parallel text containing the same command that no one should appear before the Lord empty-handed.
Detailed regulations concerning the redemption price for firstborn humans and unclean animals.
Repeats the command that no one should appear before the Lord empty-handed during the three major festivals.
Refers to the fulfillment of the law regarding the firstborn when Jesus was brought into the temple.
Theological basis: All firstborn belong to the Lord, but unclean animals and humans require redemption.
A complementary rule that defines when redemption applies and when a direct offering is required.
The historical event (the Passover lamb) which is the foundation for the requirement to redeem the firstborn.
